target_moa.text: Atrasentan is a selective endothelin type A receptor (ETA R) antagonist (>1800-fold selectivity over ETB); endothelin-1 contributes to IgAN pathogenesis, and by antagonizing ETA R atrasentan reduces proteinuria.

citations.quote: Atrasentan (Vanrafia) is a selective endothelin type A receptor (ET_A R) antagonist. Endothelin-1 is thought to contribute to the pathogenesis of immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) through vasoconstriction, platelet aggregation, immune cell migration, and extracellular matrix accumulation. By antagonizing this receptor, atrasentan reduces proteinuria.
Atrasentan is an antagonist of ET_A R with >1800-fold selectivity over endothelin type B (ET_B) (inhibition constant [K_i] = 0.034 nM versus K_i = 63.3 nM).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were peripheral edema (10% atrasentan vs 8% placebo) and anemia (7% vs 2%); also hypotension (6% vs 4%) and ALT/AST >3x ULN (2% vs 1%). Hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL was 20% vs 5%. Serious AEs in 6% (atrasentan) vs 5% (placebo). Class risks include hepatotoxicity, fluid retention, decreased sperm counts.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 5\%) with VANRAFIA were peripheral edema and anemia.

The adverse reactions that occurred more frequently in the atrasentan arm than the placebo arm were peripheral edema (10% atrasentan versus 8% placebo), anemia (7% atrasentan versus 2% placebo), hypotension (6% atrasentan versus 4% placebo), and ALT/AST >3-fold upper limit of normal (2% atrasentan versus 1% placebo)
The incidence of hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL compared to baseline was higher for the atrasentan arm (20%) compared to the placebo arm (5%).
Serious adverse events occurred in 6% of subjects in the atrasentan arm and in 5% of subjects in the placebo arm.

- Hepatotoxicity (5.2)
- Fluid Retention (5.3)
- Decreased Sperm Counts (5.4, 8.3)

detail.text: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — VANRAFIA is contraindicated in pregnant patients; it may cause major birth defects based on animal data. Exclude pregnancy before initiation and advise effective contraception.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

VANRAFIA is contraindicated for use in pregnant patients; it may cause major birth defects based on animal data [see *Contraindications* (4.1), *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1), *Use in Specific Populations* (8.1)]. Exclude pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment with VANRAFIA.

detail.text: No REMS required; the review team concluded labeling (Boxed Warning and contraception measures) is adequate to mitigate the embryo-fetal toxicity risk, and the REMS Oversight Committee agreed a REMS is not necessary.

citations.quote: Labeling will include a Boxed Warning for this risk.

the REMS Oversight Committee agreed that the embryo-fetal toxicity risk for all ERAs (including atrasentan) can be mitigated with labeling and a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefit outweighs the risk.

citations.quote: Based on the available data, the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology (the Division) accepts a substantial reduction in proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression (loss of kidney function) in IgAN and as a basis for accelerated approval (Thompson et al. 2019).
